ut_good_medicine_area.blurb: A quartzite sport wall above 10,000 feet in the Uinta Mountains, a short and easy stroll from the Ruth Lake trailhead and the first big wall you meet on the way. Nearly all of the 27 climbs are bolted single pitches, with a handful of trad lines and a lone boulder problem mixed in. Difficulty runs from the 5.7 range up into the 5.12s, but the bulk sits between 5.10 and 5.11, so strong intermediates get the most out of it. It is the busiest wall at the lake, and the cool high-country air makes it a summer refuge from the Wasatch Front heat. Expect snow on the final stretch of trail early in the season.

ut_dogwood_crag.blurb: A quartzite wall beside the creek next to the Dogwood Picnic Area, roughly a mile into Big Cottonwood Canyon. It has a mix of trad, sport, a few top-rope lines and some small boulder problems, split between a central section and an east end. The easiest lines are gentle enough for kids and first-timers, and a couple can be top-roped from a walk-up anchor, while the hard bolted lines reach into the low 5.13s. Most of the 26 climbs fall between 5.6 and 5.9. The creek keeps things cool in summer, the spot is popular and often crowded, and some protection is thin on the trad lines.

ut_thumb_area_the.blurb: The biggest single chunk of rock in Little Cottonwood Canyon, a freestanding granite summit block reached from the Gate Buttress parking. This is an all-day, multi-pitch outing rather than a quick crag visit: the lines stack cracks, slabs and faces into as many as eleven pitches, and the descent is by rappel and scrambling. Of the 26 climbs, nearly all are trad, with two aid lines and one sport route. Grades start in the easy fifth class, but most sit between 5.9 and 5.11, with a few harder. The walk in is long and tiring, over talus and brushy ledges. The slabs bake in sun, so bring water.

ut_strone_crag.blurb: A broad, mostly north-leaning quartzite wall in Big Cottonwood Canyon, sitting between Challenge Buttress and the Narcolepsy area. A big roof band across the middle gives the crag its character. It is mainly a trad venue, with 18 of its 26 climbs needing gear and the other 8 bolted, and several lines run to two or three pitches. Difficulty spans 5.6 up to the 5.12s, with a solid cluster around 5.10 and 5.11. One end catches sun while the other stays shaded longer, so there is usually a comfortable spot to climb across the season. Expect the usual canyon quartzite funk and a steep, switchbacking walk of about ten minutes.

ut_hardware_wall.blurb: A shady limestone sport crag in Left Hand Fork of Blacksmith Fork Canyon, in Cache Valley. All 25 routes are bolted, and this is a place for strong climbers: the great majority are in the 5.12 range, with a smaller group of 5.11s and several 5.13s plus one harder line. Few easy options exist, so it suits those already past the 5.11 barrier. The cliff sits a very short distance from the approach trail, and a quick stream crossing leads in. The shade makes it a pleasant choice when other limestone walls are baking.

ut_power_wall.blurb: A compact sandstone wall in Indian Creek, a smaller buttress just to the side of the Scarface cliff. All 25 routes are crack climbs protected with trad gear, and the focus is on shorter lines where smaller cams matter more than the big hand-sized pieces the Creek is known for. Most climbs fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with the center of gravity around 5.11, plus a single easier line near 5.8 for warming up. One rope handles most of the routes. It is a good stop for climbers who want finger-sized cracks and steady, pumpy climbing rather than long wide-crack sufferfests.
